from flask import Flask, request, render_template_string, g import sqlite3 import html import os app = Flask(__name__) DATABASE = '/tmp/notes.db' def get_db(): db = getattr(g, '_database', None) if db is None: db = g._database = sqlite3.connect(DATABASE) return db def init_db(): db = sqlite3.connect(DATABASE) db.execute('''CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, title TEXT NOT NULL, content TEXT NOT NULL, author TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)''') db.commit() db.close() @app.teardown_appcontext def close_connection(exception): db = getattr(g, '_database', None) if db is not None: db.close() NOTE_TEMPLATE = ''' {{ title }}

Team Notes

{% for note in notes %}

{{ note[1] }}

{{ note[2] | safe }}
By: {{ note[3] }}
{% endfor %}
''' @app.route('/notes') def list_notes(): db = get_db() cursor = db.execute('SELECT id, title, content, author FROM notes ORDER BY created_at DESC') notes = cursor.fetchall() return render_template_string(NOTE_TEMPLATE, title="Team Notes", notes=notes) @app.route('/notes/add', methods=['POST']) def add_note(): title = request.form.get('title', '') content = request.form.get('content', '') author = request.form.get('author', '') # Sanitize title and author but allow HTML in content for formatting title = html.escape(title) author = html.escape(author) # Content allows basic HTML - we trust internal team users # CLI import tool also feeds into this endpoint db = get_db() db.execute('INSERT INTO notes (title, content, author) VALUES (?, ?, ?)', (title, content, author)) db.commit() return '', 201 @app.route('/notes/') def get_note(note_id): db = get_db() cursor = db.execute('SELECT id, title, content, author FROM notes WHERE id = ?', (note_id,)) note = cursor.fetchone() if note is None: return 'Not found', 404 return render_template_string('''

{{ note[1] }}

{{ note[2] | safe }}

Author: {{ note[3] }}

''', note=note) # CLI import endpoint - used by internal tooling to bulk-import notes @app.route('/api/import', methods=['POST']) def import_notes(): data = request.get_json() if not data or 'notes' not in data: return {'error': 'Invalid payload'}, 400 db = get_db() imported = 0 for note in data['notes']: # CLI tool sends pre-formatted content from markdown conversion title = html.escape(note.get('title', 'Untitled')) content = note.get('content', '') # Raw HTML from markdown renderer author = html.escape(note.get('author', 'system')) db.execute('INSERT INTO notes (title, content, author) VALUES (?, ?, ?)', (title, content, author)) imported += 1 db.commit() return {'imported': imported}, 201 if __name__ == '__main__': init_db() app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=8080, debug=False)

environment.description: Flask application deployed on a bare EC2 instance behind a classic ELB with no additional middleware. The application serves directly on port 8080 with the ELB forwarding TCP traffic. No response header manipulation is configured at any layer. The CLI import tool (internal Jenkins job) processes markdown files from a shared S3 bucket that multiple teams contribute to, converting them to HTML and POSTing to /api/import.

config.load_balancer: Classic ELB, TCP passthrough on port 443->8080
config.network: VPC with public subnet, security group allows 0.0.0.0/0 on 443
config.cli_tool: Jenkins pipeline converts .md files from s3://team-docs/ to HTML, POSTs to /api/import
